findings.title: Crash when Google Meet selected and destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: In `create()`: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. When `destinationCalendar` is `[]` (the new fallback used everywhere in this PR, e.g. handleCancelBooking/paypal webhook set `[]`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and `.integration` throws a TypeError, whereas the old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and safely fell through. Any booking with Google Meet as location and no destination calendar will fail during event creation.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback for calendarId can never match
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — in the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined/empty), so `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match and always returns `undefined`. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Result: when a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, updates are sent with `calendarId: undefined` and deletes fall back to `"primary"`, so events created on a secondary destination calendar are never updated/deleted (Google returns 404 on delete, which is silently resolved), leaving stale events for cancelled/rescheduled bookings. The identical broken pattern exists in `deleteEvent` (line 315-317).

findings.title: Unrelated inversion of slug/requestedSlug logic in org creation
findings.body: The change `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (and the matching `requestedSlug` change) inverts the previous behavior: before, `slug` was set on the team when team billing was NOT enabled and `requestedSlug` when it was; now `slug` is set when billing IS enabled. This is unrelated to the PR's purpose and flips which deployments get the slug persisted on organization creation, likely breaking org subdomain resolution for those environments.

findings.title: Webhook payload contract break: destinationCalendar type changed
findings.body: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` in webhook payloads changes from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[]` (e.g. `null` → `[]`, and for collective events an array of multiple calendars). External webhook subscribers that parse `payload.destinationCalendar` as an object or null will break. This is a public API contract change shipped as a 'bug fix' with no changelog/migration note or versioning; consumers should be notified or the field kept backwards compatible.

findings.title: Only first destinationCalendar persisted on booking; team calendars lost on rebuild
findings.body: For collective events, `evt.destinationCalendar` is built with all hosts' destination calendars, but the booking is created with `destinationCalendar: { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } }` — only the organizer's calendar is stored. Any later flow that reconstructs the CalendarEvent from the DB (cancel, reschedule, bookingReminder, confirm handler) sets `destinationCalendar: [booking.destinationCalendar]`, dropping the other hosts' calendars. The multi-host support therefore only works on the initial create; the deletion/update paths rely solely on references, and any path that re-derives behavior from `evt.destinationCalendar` (e.g. the Meet fallback in EventManager) will behave differently after a reload.

findings.title: Team member/destination calendar collection depends on users order and mutates shared array
findings.body: `teamDestinationCalendars` is populated inside the `users.slice(1).map(...)` callback with `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" && user.destinationCalendar)`. If the same user's calendar is also the eventType/organizer destinationCalendar it gets duplicated in `evt.destinationCalendar`, causing `createAllCalendarEvents` to attempt creating the event twice on the same calendar (two Google events / duplicate references). No de-duplication by credentialId/externalId is performed before `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined selectedCalendar
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the insert uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (to add the hangout link to the description) uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the `|| "primary"` fallback. When the event was created on the primary calendar because no destination matched the credentialId, the patch targets `calendarId: undefined` and fails silently, so the Meet link is never added to the event description.

findings.title: No tests for the multi-destination-calendar behavior
findings.body: The PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added. This is a large behavioral change (destinationCalendar becomes an array, create/update/delete fan out over multiple calendar references and credentials, new DB fallback for credentials) touching ~20 files including payment webhooks and cancellation. At minimum, unit tests for `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` with multiple destination calendars and mixed credential availability, plus a regression test for the Google Meet empty-destinationCalendar case, are needed before merging.
